Syrian antiquities were also returned to their homeland to once again take their place in Syria's museums. And in Ankara, His Excellency President Ahmad al-Assad met with the President of the United States, Donald Trump, and received from him a letter confirming the decision to inform the U.S. Congress to begin procedures for removing Syria from the list of state sponsors of terrorism. This is a historic decision that removes one of the last barriers left by the former regime between Syria and the world for decades. Dear colleagues, the world is no longer— is not just returning to Syria through political and economic delegations, but people themselves have returned. And I am not simply referring to returnees and refugees, but I will speak speak of tourists. The Ministry of Tourism announced today that during the first half of this year, the country received 3.52 million visitors, while the number of foreign tourists increased by 448%. These are not simply indicators, but these are signs of confidence in a country that is reclaiming its placed on the map of the world. Madam President, the picture today is clearer than ever. Syria is sending rescue teams. Meanwhile, Israel sends occupying forces. Syria seizes smuggled weapons while Israel crosses borders carrying weapons. Syria extinguishes fires while Syria ignites them. And as you heard, Syria is working on and welcoming the United Nations while Israel is obstructing its humanitarian convoys. While Syria is working to protect its people and to strengthen security and stability in the region, Netanyahu places his narrow electoral calculations above the region's security. He misleads his people and deceives them into believing that more wars will bring them more safety. Thus, he is pushing his people into from one battle into the other with no horizon and with no end in sight. Colleagues, Syria has chosen diplomacy and restraint. It has chosen to move forward through the appreciated American initiative. We are fully aware that dialogue. does not mean accepting occupation, and diplomacy does not mean relinquishing our rights. In closing, Madam President, we had the pleasure months ago to host you in Damascus in a milestone visit that was important in Syria's relationship with Security Council. Today, Damascus looks forward to welcoming the Secretary-General of the United Nations in a visit that will be far more than a protocol stop. Rather, it will bear witness— live witness— to a historic transformation forged by Syrians, men and women, through their determination and through their sacrifice. Syria has appeared before this Council for a long time as an intractable crisis. Today, however, it returns to the Council as a story of success. Welcome to the Secretary-General in Damascus. We welcome him in a Syria that has regained its voice and its place and its future. I thank you, Madam President.
I thank the representative of the Syrian Arab Republic for this statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Türkiye.

Thank you, Madam President. We thank the distinguished briefers for their comprehensive presentations. We welcome the recent announcement regarding UN Secretary-General's visit to Syria and thank His Excellency Guterres for his strong commitment. Madam President, Syria has maintained positive momentum toward greater stability. Since the Council's last meeting under this agenda item, there have been several encouraging developments. First and foremost, we warmly welcome the convening of the People's Assembly in Syria on the 12th of July. Bringing together the various segments of Syrian society, the Assembly will make a valuable contribution in establishing stability, security and prosperity through inclusive governance. It will also enable the adoption of the legislation the country needs to accelerate its reconstruction process. The election of a woman MP as one of the 2 Deputy Speakers of the People's Assembly is another positive progress for the future of women's political participation and representation Syria. During the recent visit of President Chara to Ankara, which coincided with the NATO Summit, President Trump announced his intention to rescind Syria's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism. Once realized, this step will contribute greatly to international efforts in support of Syria's reconstruction and recovery. A further significant development was the reinstatement of Syria's suspended rights and privileges under the Chemical Weapons Convention. This clearly demonstrates the success of Syria's national efforts undertaken in cooperation with the international community on the chemical weapons file. Madam President, these positive steps, however, continue to be exposed to significant risks. The terrorist attacks that took place in Damascus on the 2nd and 7th of July were clear attempts to undermine the progress achieved towards durable stability and social cohesion. We are confident that the Syrian people will give the most effective response to such provocations by preserving their unity and solidarity. These latest attacks also underscore that the threat emanating from Daesh must be monitored closely and continuously. Support to reinforce Syria's counterterrorism capacity should therefore continue. At the same time, the situation in the south remains a source of grave concern. Israel's continued attacks directly targeting civilian life, including the recent raids in western Daraa where 2 children were wounded, constitute a clear violation of international law and the 1974 Separation of Forces Agreement. The international community should fulfill its responsibilities in bringing an end to these attacks that hinder both the progress Syria has achieved since December 2024 and the stability of the entire region. The swift and uninterrupted conclusion of the integration of the northeast should likewise remain high on the national agenda. Madam President, the international community must step up its support for Syria's recovery and reconstruction, including through sustained and predictable financing. These efforts require close coordination with the Syrian authorities and the United Nations. The rehabilitation of the critical infrastructure remains amongst the most urgent priorities. While humanitarian assistance must continue to reach those in need, it should increasingly be complemented by early recovery and development support. Turkey continues to contribute actively in sectors where targeted investments can generate significant multiplier effects. In conclusion, Madam President, Turkey remains firmly committed to supporting Syria's unity, sovereignty, territorial integrity, stability, and prosperity, And we will continue to work with all partners towards this end. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Turkey for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of the Observer State of Palestine.

Madam President, at the outset, I would like to thank you. for convening this meeting on the political and humanitarian situation in the Syrian Arab Republic. I would also like to thank the briefers, and I have the honor to deliver this statement on behalf of the Arab Group. Dear colleagues, the Arab Group reiterates its support to the unity, sovereignty, and territorial integrity of Syria and supported to the efforts of the Syrian government to exercise control over its entire territory. And it— the group calls on the international community to support the efforts of the Syrian government to maintain stability in Syria as a critical step to maintain security and stability in the region. Madam President, the Arab Group welcomes the decision of His Excellency the President of the United States, Mr. Donald Trump, To start the formal measures to remove Syria from the list of terrorist— terror-sponsoring states. Syria has been listed decades ago as a result of the activities of the previous regime. It is an important step to accelerate the economic recovery. In this connection, the Arab Group calls on all states to accompany Syria in its reforms and the major economic transformations by reinforcing their investments and contributing to building a new, prosperous, and safe Syria. In this regard, we reiterate the important role of the United Nations, and we call for playing an important— a bigger role in the development of Syria consistent with Syria's vision of its national priorities. Madam President, the Arab Group condemns in the strongest words the heinous terrorist acts that targeted Syria recently and calls on the international community to support efforts of Syria in fighting ISIS and terrorism in all its forms to achieve security and stability in the region and eradicate the threat of terrorism. Madam President, the Arab Group commends the positive development in Syria's relations with different countries in the region and the world. The group reiterates the importance of concerted international efforts to provide tangible support to Syria in its critical transitional phase, and the group stresses the important role of the UN in this regard. The group calls on the international community, the UN, and its specialized agencies to provide different kinds of support to the Syrian government and cooperate with the government in its efforts to achieve economic recovery, reconstruction, and creating safe environment as well as providing the necessary conditions for the sustainable, voluntary, and dignified return of Syrian refugees. In this regard, the Arab Group expresses its deep appreciation to the major role played by refugees' hosting countries, and we call on the international community to promote and expand the support to these countries. For these countries should not and may not be left to shoulder this heavy humanitarian and economic responsibilities alone. Dear colleagues, against the backdrop of the severe humanitarian consequences as a result of the 14-year-long war in Syria, in particular, the mines and explosive remnants of war, the Arab Group calls on the United Nations and the international community to reinforce— to join forces and support efforts of the Syrian government in this important field to protect civilians and create a safe environment for recovery and return of population, as well as improving living conditions of the Syrian people. Madam President, the Arab Group condemns in, in the strongest terms the repeated Israeli incursions into and attacks on the Syrian territories. They constitute flagrant violation to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria and blatant breach of the provisions of the UN Charter and international law, and threat to the security and stability of Syria and peace and security in the region. The Arab Group underscores the importance of compelling Israel to fully uphold the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, and the group calls Israel to end its repeated attacks and calls for immediate and unconditional withdrawal from Syrian territories and from the entire occupied Syrian Golan and immediate end of its illegal settlement activities. In conclusion, Madam President, the Arab Group reiterates its steadfast solidarity with the sisterly Syria at its critical moment of its history. and its path towards a secure, stable, and prosperous future of Syria based on justice, equality, and rule of law, and ensures the rights and dignity of all Syrians. Thank you.
I thank the representative of the Observer State of Palestine for their statement. There are no more names. Inscribed on the list of speakers. The meeting is adjourned.
